discrepancies.severity: load-bearing evidence-record defect (claim survives, artifact does not)
discrepancies.claim: State 'CME legacy ... contract-specification page for Corn' asserts inside its verbatim field '[2015-05-22, seventeen days before the TAS launch] zero occurrences of TAS', and the encodable repeats 'the corn spec page has zero TAS at 2014-11-02 and 2015-05-22'.
discrepancies.finding: pass2/corn-legacy-20150522230148.html is not a CME page. Its title is '<title>Wayback Machine</title>' and it flattens to 3,718 characters of Internet Archive chrome with no 'Corn Futures', no 'Trading Hours' and no 'Product Code'. The zero-TAS count was computed over archive boilerplate. Its recorded sha256 does match the file, so this is a mis-read artifact rather than a fabricated one, and the file passes SHA256SUMS.txt - the hash discipline cannot catch this class of error on its own.
discrepancies.impact: The citation as it stands is vacuous. I re-fetched the same URL and timestamp today: Wayback CDX shows 20150522230148 as a real 200 capture (digest 6HB5XFH6EGKXEU62EAUJXJ4SLMQ26J2Z) and the replay returns an 83,721-byte CME spec page (sha256 fd5f67b3a740beeff5e98028cfa5ac7de244189d12ac90589cac850de8520ba3, saved as verify-pass/v_corn20150522.html) with 0 case-sensitive 'TAS' and the pre-move outright 'Monday - Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 1:15 p.m. CT'. So the substantive claim is true on bytes I fetched, not on bytes the researcher held. Replace the stored artifact before the 2015-05-22 citation reaches a source comment.

discrepancies.severity: invented string inside a verbatim field
discrepancies.claim: The wiki state's verbatim block reads 'Products Not In Scope | The following spot quoted futures products will remain on a 5 day trading schedule. [QBTC, ...]'.
discrepancies.finding: The sentence and the twelve product codes are verbatim. The heading is not: the wiki's heading is 'Product Scope'. 'not in scope' occurs zero times in either saved version of the page.
discrepancies.impact: Cosmetic for the conclusion - the exclusion list is real and the TAS books are not in it - but the gate's evidence discipline requires verbatim fields to be byte-exact, and this one would be copied into a source comment as a quotation.

discrepancies.severity: load-bearing encoding-specification defect - would publish an unsourced session
discrepancies.claim: encodable: 'ROW 2 - 2026-05-29. 24/7 with maintenance Saturday 02:00-04:00 CT and Monday-Friday 15:00-15:05 CT'; residual A: the day-one question is 'a ONE-DAY question, therefore a LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE date exception rather than a template row'.
discrepancies.finding: Two problems. (i) A single day-level row at 2026-05-29 carrying the steady-state 24/7 grid asserts that the crypto TAS book was open from Friday local midnight and reopened that Friday at 15:05 - and the researcher's own residual A says nothing retrieved states whether it reopened at 15:05, 16:02 or 16:30. It also rewrites the era-1 Thursday-17:00-to-Friday-15:00 leg as a Friday-midnight open, which is precisely the running session LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES says a day-level boundary must not split. (ii) LAW-HOLIDAY-SCOPE scopes date exceptions to holidays - an early final close, a late first open, or a closure - not to a migration's first day, which is a real, sourced, persistent change to the recurring week that arrives mid-day. The crate does not route the identical event to DayPolicy for the futures key: cryptocurrency.rs carries (2026,5,29,&TRANSITION_2026_05_29,'CME filing 26-114') then (2026,5,30,&CURRENT,'CME filing 26-114'), with the comment 'The permanent 24/7 normal week did not govern the morning of its first day ... Keeping this one-day bridge prevents the historical Thursday open from being rewritten as Friday midnight.'
discrepancies.impact: Follow the futures precedent: a bridge row at 2026-05-29 that keeps the Thursday-17:00 leg and withholds the unsourced Friday-afternoon reopen, then the steady-state row at 2026-05-30. The era boundary itself is firm and the researcher is right about that; only the row shape is wrong.

discrepancies.severity: load-bearing encoding-specification defect - reports a sourced phase as absent
discrepancies.claim: encodable, crypto TAS: no order_entry rules are specified, and the residual list names only the grain TAS Pre-Open (B) and the pre-2016 livestock TAS Pre-Open (C) as undated queues.
discrepancies.finding: The crypto TAS Pre-Open is sourced by the same wiki table the era-2 executable grid comes from: 'Pre-open: 3:01:30 p.m. to 3:04:30 p.m. CT No cancel: 3:04:30 p.m. to 3:05:00 p.m. CT' on Monday through Friday, and 'Pre-open: 3:45:30 a.m. to 3:59:30 a.m. CT No cancel: 3:59:30 a.m. to 4:00:00 a.m. CT' on Saturday. cryptocurrency.rs encodes the analogous Saturday 03:45 phase for the futures key from the same channel. Dropping it silently leaves a reader to infer it is unsourced when it is stated in the operator's own table.
discrepancies.impact: Either encode the era-2 queue windows or say explicitly beside the table that they were withheld and why. This is an order-entry gap, the lower-priority kind under the crate's executable-windows-first rule, but the defect is the false 'nothing sourced' impression, not the omission itself.

discrepancies.claim: encodable, livestock ROW 3: 'key 2020-05-31 ... Source SER-8599R, which names LET/GFT/HET with both values.'
discrepancies.finding: SER-8599R reads 'Effective Sunday, May 31, 2020 for trade date Monday, June 1, 2020, and pending all relevant regulatory CFTC review periods'. It is conditional. The researcher discharges the identical clause explicitly for SER-7591 (fact card created 2016-03-03, spec page 2016-03-11) but records no discharge for SER-8599R; the only warrant offered is that livestock.rs already keys 2020-05-31 to it.
discrepancies.impact: That precedent is real and I confirmed it, so the row is defensible, but under LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES the discharge has to be recorded beside the row rather than assumed. No post-effective artifact for this row was retrieved on either pass.

discrepancies.claim: dead_ends #5: 'The ag TAS fact card has exactly three editions in its entire archived life (CDX: three distinct 200-status digests ...). No fourth edition hides an intermediate grain or livestock state.'
discrepancies.finding: The three-digest count is exact - I re-ran the CDX. But the archive has a five-year hole in this URL between 20150616064756 and 20200608032955, and we know an edition was created inside that hole (CreationDate 2016-03-03) and first captured only in 2020. The CDX therefore supports 'no fourth edition survives in the archive', not 'no fourth edition existed'.
discrepancies.impact: None for the conclusion: the grain TAS window is independently observed at 2015-09-05, 2015-10-09, 2016-03-10, 2017-05-20, 2019-07-17 and then 2021-07-10 onward, and the livestock TAS window at 2016-03-11, 2017-12-11 and 2021-07-10 onward. Fix the wording so the next reader does not treat the CDX as proof of the operator's publishing history.

discrepancies.claim: Several verbatim fields are reordered or elided composites.
discrepancies.finding: The trading-hours-service block opens with ZCT although the response's first product is KET; the fact-card key-feature line is quoted as 'TAS order entry is not allowed prior to the beginning of each group's pre-open state' where the document continues ', just like other order types'; the 26-114 and SER-9740R Table 1 quotes are bracketed elisions. All substrings are in the bytes and no time, date, zone or product code is misstated.

discrepancies.severity: minor - internal inconsistency in the encoding spec
discrepancies.claim: livestock ROW 1 is keyed 2015-06-08 ('no wrap, so the Monday trade date is the opening day') while ROW 3 is keyed 2020-05-31 (the Sunday effective day, 'matches how livestock.rs keys the same change').
discrepancies.finding: Both cannot follow from one rule. The grid has no Sunday session in either era, so the two keyings are observationally identical and neither is wrong; but the handwritten HISTORICAL_CUTOVERS expectations need one stated convention.
discrepancies.impact: Pick the livestock.rs convention for both and say so, or state the divergence beside the table.

residual_caveats: Only the CORN legacy spec page carries the family sentence. sb-legacy-20150905.html, captured the same day, prints 'TAS: SBT' in Product Code and the outright 13:20 but no TAS hours sentence at all. The six-root grain family claim therefore rests on the corn page's own scope phrase ('all CBOT Grain TAS products') plus the fact card's single six-root cell - which is what the researcher says, and it must be said that way beside the table.

globex_grains_tas spans three Globex security groups (TA/TP/TW, confirmed from CME's own service). The family claim is textual, not structural; keep the researcher's instruction to state it beside the table.

The livestock era-1 fact-card hours cell carries no zone label ('Monday, 9:05 a.m. - 1 p.m. / Tuesday - Friday, 8 a.m. - 1 p.m.'); the CT reading comes from the live-cattle spec page's 'Chicago time'. Cite the spec page, not the fact card, for era 1's zone.

Observation gaps exist inside both ag eras - grain TAS 2019-07-17 to 2021-07-10, livestock TAS 2017-12-11 to 2021-07-10 - with the same state at both ends. Asserting no revision is the right treatment (it declines to invent a date), but 'no gap wide enough to hide a revision' is rhetoric, not a measurement.

CME Rulebook Chapter 5 / Rule 524 is a channel the dead_ends list does not mention. I opened it: 524.A.1 confirms a TAS-eligible contract has a 'prescribed pre-open time period' but states no clock time, and the TAS/BTIC/TACO/TMAC Table is served as an external XLS. It does not close residual B (the grain TAS Pre-Open onset) and should be added to the exhausted-channel list rather than left for the next reader to try.

The 16:01-16:02 CT crypto TAS pause is a live CME-vs-CME conflict, not a gap, and the researcher's treatment matches the ECBTC precedent: serve open 15:05->16:01 and 16:02->15:00, withhold the disputed minute by serving it closed. The encodable's own prose states this twice in a self-contradictory order ('open 15:05 -> 15:00 next day ... and withhold the disputed 16:01-16:02 minute by treating it as closed'); the operative instruction is the second clause and should be the only one written.
U-4 (regular vs extended) is untouched by this gate for all three keys and is the only residual touching an executable-window classification.
crypto-tas-page-20251220093441.html in the evidence directory is undecompressed gzip and unreadable as saved. It is cited in no state, so nothing rests on it.

The 2026/5 filing sweep was spot-checked, not re-run end to end: 26-113, 26-115, 26-117 and 26-120 all return CME's 404 page through the reader, consistent with the report. The decisive negative - zero 'TAS' in 26-114, SER-9740 and SER-9740R - was fully re-verified, and SER-9740R was re-fetched independently today.
